name: Burning Witch
label: Southern Lord
lede: Burning Witch lasted about three years, played to rooms that emptied by the second song, and cut two EPs, one with Steve Albini at the board. Sunn O))), Goatsnake and Khanate all trace back to it.

eras.title: Out of the Thorr's Hammer wreckage
eras.text: Thorr's Hammer lasted about six weeks. Its guitarists wanted music slower and lower than anything left over from Seattle's grunge years, and they found a singer who could scream over it.

years.src: Wikipedia: Thorr's Hammer · Southern Lord · The Sleeping Shaman
years.h: Thorr's Hammer folds, and Burning Witch grows out of it
years.p: Guitarist Stephen O'Malley, guitarist Greg Anderson and Jamie Sykes carry on once Norwegian vocalist Runhild Gammelsæter goes back to Oslo. Wikipedia calls Burning Witch an offshoot of Thorr's Hammer.
years.xp:
Thorr's Hammer formed in Seattle's Ballard neighborhood in winter 1994–95, played two shows and recorded a demo and the Dommedagsnatt EP. Burning Witch started on Capitol Hill with the same core.

Sources differ on who played what. Wikipedia lists Sykes on bass at first, while Edgy 59 remembers him on drums.

years.h: A bassist and a singer who met over a car
years.p: G. Stuart Dahlquist on bass and Edgar Livengood, who sings as Edgy 59, complete the band. Edgy 59's voice swings between nasal melody and tortured screams.
years.xp:
Edgy 59 says he met Dahlquist while working on his car: "He liked my car and we began a friendship." Dahlquist brought O'Malley and Anderson to a JUNKHALO show, and by Edgy 59's account Burning Witch started about a week later.

He had heard of Thorr's Hammer but never heard them, and he says he skipped their shows because he disliked low, guttural vocals.

years.h: Anderson heads for Los Angeles to start Goatsnake
years.p: Southern Lord says Anderson left soon after for LA to launch [[Goatsnake|ae720a02-629e-4e9b-98e7-d1f637bd5a49]], leaving O'Malley to lead the band. Wikipedia says he was gone before anything was recorded.
years.xp: Anderson later founded the Southern Lord label, which would release the band's compilation. He and O'Malley kept working together, most visibly in [[Sunn O)))|1d3da898-4fb4-4445-b704-cd7315e01789]].

eras.title: Albini, and the empty rooms
eras.text: The band tracked its first EP with a famous engineer, swapped drummers, and played to crowds that thinned out by the second song.

years.h: Steve Albini records them at Robert Lang Studios
years.p: The songs that become the Towers... EP are tracked in Shoreline, Washington, with [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] producing.
years.xp:
Edgy 59 says Albini recorded them as a favor to an old friend of Dahlquist's. He adds that Albini's magazine Descent never promoted the band.

The songs then sat unreleased for two years.

years.src: Southern Lord · Wikipedia · The Sleeping Shaman
years.h: Sykes goes back to England, B.R.A.D. takes the drums
years.p: After the Albini sessions Jamie Sykes leaves, and B.R.A.D. plays drums on Rift.Canyon.Dreams.
years.xp: Edgy 59 says Sykes left to move back to England, and that B.R.A.D.'s arrival gave the band "a more conceptual" and less sludgy feel.

years.big: "By the second song there were 10 people left"
q: Halfway into the opening song the house was one quarter full.
years.h: Down to ten people by the second song
years.p: Edgy 59 on playing Seattle in 1997. A quarter-full room at the start of the opener was nearly empty ten minutes later.
years.xp:
He says the band shared bills with Napalm Death, At the Gates and Boris. His answer to the thinning crowd was to stay focused on his own performance.

A 1997 Seattle set, filmed in full and posted by Southern Lord, survives.

years.h: Rift.Canyon.Dreams goes down at Robert Lang Studios
years.p: O'Malley, Dahlquist, B.R.A.D. and Edgy 59 cut four songs, among them "Warning Signs" and "Communion".
years.xp: Wikipedia says Merciless Records pressed 500 copies. It describes the EP as more morose and brooding than Towers....

eras.title: Two EPs, then the end
eras.text: Both EPs reach vinyl and disc in 1998, around the time the band stops. Sources disagree on exactly when it stopped.

years.p: The 1996 Albini session becomes a 12-inch of about 37 minutes, two years after it was recorded.

years.h: Crippled Lucifer puts both EPs on Southern Lord
years.p: Seven tracks, 63 minutes, on [[Greg Anderson|a8da7651-6d6f-4021-98a6-d68b35b1e4f8]]'s label. Wikipedia says printing errors on the first cover led to several pressings.
play: Crippled Lucifer (Seven Psalms for Our Lord of Light)

years.src: Southern Lord · Wikipedia · The Sleeping Shaman
years.p: Southern Lord says the band reunited briefly for autumn 1998 shows. Wikipedia says it split that fall, after the last ones.
years.xp: Edgy 59 tells it differently. He says O'Malley decided to move to Europe in 1997 and the band called it quits, and that he started Sinisstar a month or so later.

eras.title: Everybody goes somewhere louder
eras.text: The members scatter into bands that grow much bigger than Burning Witch ever was, and the old recordings keep circulating on splits and a deluxe reissue.

years.h: Goatsnake and Burning Witch share a split CD on Hydra Head
years.p: Burning Witch adds "Communion" and "The Bleeder" to a split with Anderson's new band.

years.h: Asva gets the other side of a 12-inch
years.p: The Dos Fatales split carries a Burning Witch take on "Rift Canyon Dreams", remixed by Randall Dunn.
years.xp: Dahlquist and B.R.A.D. both later played in Asva.

years.h: Crippled Lucifer comes back as a double CD
years.p: Southern Lord's reissue restores a missing track and adds the split songs. It was delayed from January 25.
He and Anderson formed Sunn O))), with Dahlquist on its first two albums. Edgy 59 went to Sinisstar.
